title: Microbilling matrix: token-level charge attribution, breakdown, and CSV export workflow
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Design an actionable, exportable token-level cost view that helps engineers and finance teams reconcile inference charges by route, model variant, and user/customer attribution. Scope: interactive matrix/table UI in Redwood Console for time-range queries, multi-dimension grouping (route, model, customer_id, tag), per-token breakdown (prompt vs. completion vs. system tokens), and first-class CSV/JSONL export for downstream reconciliation. The design must balance dense analytics (for power users) with guided defaults for product teams. Constraints: limited screen real-estate, performance of in-browser pivoting for large query windows, and strict privacy constraints for customer identifiers. Stakeholders: billing PM (Ravi Kapoor), backend lead (Priya Nayar), analytics (Sofia Morales), legal/compliance for exports (Erik Jensen). Acceptance criteria: (1) user can pivot by at least three dimensions and see token and cost columns; (2) export schema documented and signed off by finance; (3) prototype passes accessibility audit; (4) eng validates API fields required for export. Success metrics: adoption by top 5 customers for reconciliation flows, reduction in billing-support tickets about per-token discrepancies by 40% in the quarter after launch.
comments: 2026-02-14 - Ava Martinez: Initial sketches posted in Figma. Two layout options: dense matrix (spreadsheet-first) vs guided cards (summary-first). Shared with Ravi and Priya for feasibility review.

2026-02-17 - Ravi Kapoor (PM): Likes the matrix for power users; asks for a default saved view aimed at finance that hides PII and aggregates by customer alias. Requests export column order to match accounting ledger column names.

2026-02-21 - Priya Nayar (Eng): Backend can return per-token attribution but will need pagination and stream export endpoints; suggests server-side aggregation for >1M token windows. Notes a required API change: add 'charge_source' and 'cost_component' fields.

2026-02-25 - Linus Chen (Design): Iterated prototype to include a compact pivot rail, column-visibility toggles, and an export modal with schema preview. Added sample CSV and JSONL templates in Confluence.

2026-02-27 - Sofia Morales (Analytics): Suggested an additional column for 'KV cache hits' to allow more accurate amortized cost models. Recommends including quantization profile tags to surface cost regression.

2026-03-01 - QA note: Accessibility review flagged low contrast on small numeric chips and missing keyboard shortcuts for pivot focus. Design updated to meet AA contrast and added keyboard interactions.
2026-03-02 - Ava Martinez: Submitted for design review. Uploaded Figma link and Confluence spec. Next: sign-off with Priya for API contract, and PM approval on export schema.
decisions: Choose a spreadsheet-like primary view (matrix) with an optional summary card panel to serve both power users and ops.
Exports will be offered as CSV (default) and JSONL for engineering integrations; CSV column order will be configurable and have a 'finance template' preset.
Default grouping will be by route -> model -> customer_alias; users can reorder and save named views.
Large-range queries (>1M tokens) will use server-side aggregation and a streamed export endpoint to avoid front-end memory limits.
PII removal: exports default to customer_alias; raw identifiers require entitlement check and explicit PM/legal sign-off.

Finance to approve CSV 'finance template' columns and column names by 2026-03-06.
